lesson_title: Correction and reflection: testing and debugging

rubric.exceeds: A documented revision traces symptom to cause to fix to passing check, and a pattern across errors is named with a countermeasure.
rubric.meets: At least one real revision is documented with what changed and how improvement can be told.
rubric.developing: A change was made but the cause or the evidence of improvement is missing.
rubric.beginning: No evidence the work was revisited or corrected.

rubric.exceeds: Every claim or choice is backed by specific evidence or clearly explained reasoning a reader can follow unaided.
rubric.meets: Most claims or choices are backed by evidence or reasoning, with only small gaps.
rubric.developing: Some claims are supported but several are asserted without support.
rubric.beginning: Claims are asserted with little or no supporting evidence or reasoning.

rubric.exceeds: The record shows the actual working order, including abandoned attempts and dead ends, in enough detail to reconstruct the session.
rubric.meets: The required log, trace, or notes are present and record what was done and why.
rubric.developing: Documentation exists but is thin, out of order, or written after the fact from memory.
rubric.beginning: Little or no record of the process was kept.

scoring_judgment_guidance: Score this session with the rubric below, not against a fixed answer key — a design, code, or debugging task legitimately has more than one valid solution. Score only what a correction and reflection on testing and debugging can show: this is one increment of progress, so score the increment and its documentation rather than the unfinished whole. Record the level reached on each dimension with one specific reason drawn from the actual submission. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about testing and debugging.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about testing and debugging; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use digital artifact, algorithm or code, test log, source record, design explanation, and safe-use reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence/reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

unit_assessment_reference.note: This lesson is one session inside the unit; the unit assessment record above is the summative instrument, and this lesson rubric scores only this session's evidence.

remediation_plan: Reteaching for testing and debugging follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for testing and debugging, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for testing and debugging works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of testing and debugging, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking testing and debugging mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension_plan: Apply testing and debugging under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on testing and debugging rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can do this with the keyboard only, no mouse needed. Text can be made bigger, and you may do it on paper instead of a screen.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.

safety_and_privacy.note: No real credential, live external system, production account, or real personal data is used anywhere in this session; all values are fictional or sandboxed and no live system may be probed or accessed.
